basic_details.job_title: IIT Indore Junior Research Fellow/Project Associate I Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online
basic_details.short_information: The Department of Metallurgical Engineering and Materials Science at the Indian Institute of Technology Indore has invited applications for one (01) Junior Research Fellow (JRF)/Project Associate-I (PA-I) post under the externally sponsored project "Development of Mo-free Duplex Stainless Steel", funded by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF). JRF (with GATE/NET) gets ₹37,000 per month + HRA (as per norms) and Project Associate-I (without GATE/NET) gets ₹25,000 per month + HRA (as per DST/ANRF norms). content_sections.heading: IIT Indore Recruitment 2026 at a Glance
content_sections.text: The official notification does not specify the application fee.

rows.details: Development of Mo-free Duplex Stainless Steel
Initially one year, extendable up to three years; co-terminus with the project
JRF: ₹37,000 per month + HRA; Project Associate-I: ₹25,000 per month + HRA

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Candidates holding any one of the following qualifications are eligible: Candidates must have obtained First Division or an equivalent CGPA/CPI, as defined by the awarding Institute/University. Candidates with a valid GATE score or a qualified national-level examination (CSIR-UGC NET, DST-INSPIRE, etc.) will be considered for the post of JRF. Candidates without GATE/NET qualification are also eligible to apply and will be considered for the position of Project Associate-I. Candidates with interest and/or experience in one or more of these areas are encouraged to apply: Mechanical behaviour of materials, including high-temperature deformation studies. Materials characterization techniques (XRD, SEM, TEM, EBSD, etc.). Computational modelling (e.g., ABAQUS or other finite element analysis software). Thermodynamic and phase stability analysis (e.g., Thermo-Calc). Corrosion behaviour of metallic materials. Experimental materials processing, including melting, casting, heat treatment and thermo-mechanical processing. The age limit is maximum 32 years. Age relaxation is applicable as per Government of India norms for SC/ST/OBC/Women/PwD candidates. The notice does not mention a cut-off date for counting age. The notice does not list further discipline-wise conditions; for the full eligibility, refer to the official notification.

rows.essential_qualification: M.E./M.Tech./M.S. in Metallurgy/Materials Science and Engineering/Mechanical Engineering/Manufacturing Engineering/Production Engineering/Nanotechnology/Engineering Science/Engineering Physics/Ceramics Engineering/Electronics/Chemical Engineering/Energy Science and Engineering or a related discipline
B.E./B.Tech. in the same list of disciplines or a related discipline
M.Sc. in Chemistry/Physics/Materials Science or a related discipline

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The engagement is initially for one year and is extendable up to three years based on satisfactory performance. The position is co-terminus with the project. The selected candidate will be strongly encouraged to register for the Ph.D. programme at IIT Indore, subject to fulfilling the Institute's admission requirements.

rows.fellowship: ₹25,000/- per month + HRA (as per DST/ANRF norms)

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for IIT Indore Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Prepare a detailed CV/resume. Gather copies of academic marksheets/degree certificates, and the GATE scorecard or other qualifying examination/fellowship certificates, if available. Email them to Dr. Chandan Halder, Assistant Professor, Department of Metallurgical Engineering and Materials Science, Indian Institute of Technology Indore, at [email protected] . Write the email subject exactly as: Application for JRF under ANRF Project. Send the email on or before 20 November 2026.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted via email for the interview. The interview is tentatively scheduled to be conducted online during the last week of November 2026. The notice gives no exact interview date.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in IIT Indore Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There is one (01) post of Junior Research Fellow (JRF)/Project Associate-I (PA-I) in the Department of Metallurgical Engineering and Materials Science.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for the IIT Indore JRF post?
faq.answer: The last date for application is 20 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for IIT Indore JRF/Project Associate-I?
faq.answer: Candidates need M.E./M.Tech./M.S. or B.E./B.Tech. in the listed engineering and science disciplines or a related discipline, or M.Sc. in Chemistry/Physics/Materials Science or a related discipline, with First Division or an equivalent CGPA/CPI.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: The maximum age is 32 years, with relaxation as per Government of India norms for SC/ST/OBC/Women/PwD candidates.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary for the IIT Indore JRF post?
faq.answer: JRF (with GATE/NET) receives ₹37,000/- per month + HRA (as per norms). Project Associate-I (without GATE/NET) receives ₹25,000/- per month + HRA (as per DST/ANRF norms).

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply for IIT Indore JRF Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Email your detailed CV and copies of marksheets/degree certificates and GATE or other qualifying certificates, if available, to [email protected] with the subject "Application for JRF under ANRF Project".

faq.question: Q7. How are candidates selected?
faq.answer: Only shortlisted candidates are contacted by email for an interview, tentatively online in the last week of November 2026.

faq.question: Q8. Can I apply without a GATE or NET score?
faq.answer: Yes. Candidates without GATE/NET are eligible and will be considered for the position of Project Associate-I.

faq.question: Q9. Is HRA paid on top of the fellowship?
faq.answer: Yes. Both amounts are stated as per month + HRA: as per norms for JRF and as per DST/ANRF norms for Project Associate-I.

faq.question: Q10. How long is the engagement?
faq.answer: It is initially for one year, extendable up to three years based on satisfactory performance, and is co-terminus with the project.
